speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand your condition better, tell me: do you have trouble passing stool, and has your urine output decreased recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal atresia.
The presence of abdominal distension, crying upon palpation (tenderness), and feeding difficulties in an 8-month-old suggests a surgical abdominal emergency. While the age is atypical for classic presentations of atresia which usually occur earlier, the clinical picture of a distended, tender abdomen with vomiting or feeding refusal warrants immediate surgical evaluation.
